newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Vietnam considers joining coffee group - minister.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam considers joining coffee group - minister.

text.p: Vietnam supports the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) and will consider joining the coffee producers group, said the Ivorian minister for commodities Guy-Alain Gauze.
"Vietnam has expressed its support for the ACPC and said it will consider at a government level joining the ACPC," Gauze told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Gauze has just returned from a visit to Vietnam where he met the vice-minister of Foreign Affairs.
"It was a very successful meeting. Vietnam is also concerned about current robusta coffee prices," Gauze said.

Gauze is in Rio de Janeiro prior to a meeting of the ACPC on January 23 in which producers will discuss cutting exports for the January to June 1997 period. Vietnam may even send an observer to the meeting, Gauze said.
He declined to say when Vietnam may consider joining the ACPC.
Other major robusta producers like Indonesia have expressed reluctance to consider further export cuts without the participation of Vietnam in the ACPC.
